profile.reading:
This is the Centro Elaborazione Dati Catocci Bianciardi, a small third party data processing bureau at Via del Paradiso 41 in Siena, Italy, formally registered as S.A.S. Centro Elaborazione Dati Catocci Bianciardi di Bari Simone, Bianciardi Susanna e Vanni Serena, a limited partnership. This registry's operator label, Bari Bianciardi Vanni, reflects the surnames of the business's three partners, Simone Bari, Susanna Bianciardi and Serena Vanni, rather than a place name, and the business is located in Siena rather than in the city of Bari, a correction this registry records directly.

Italian business registry records show the partnership was incorporated on 1 February 1994 and classify its activity under ATECO code 63102, elaborazione dati per conto terzi, meaning data processing on behalf of third parties. That is the classic small town Italian data processing bureau, a business model common from the 1970s onward, handling outsourced payroll, accounting and similar back office work for local firms that did not keep their own computing staff. The business is currently listed with a single employee, consistent with a small long established local service provider rather than a modern colocation or wholesale data centre.

The confusion that put this row into a data centre registry is a translation problem rather than a mapping error. In Italian commercial usage a centro elaborazione dati, usually abbreviated CED, is a bookkeeping and payroll service bureau, and the phrase appears in thousands of Italian company names of exactly this kind. Rendered into English as data centre and matched against the OpenStreetMap telecom tag, it produces a facility record where a two room professional office actually stands.

The provenance supports that reading. The OpenStreetMap object is a single point rather than a building outline, created in June 2024 by one contributor who entered the trading name, street address, telephone number and the telecom data centre tag together in a single edit, the pattern of someone transcribing a business directory listing rather than surveying a facility.

Siena is a historic Tuscan city built on tourism, its medieval university and its banking heritage, home to Monte dei Paschi di Siena, one of the world's oldest surviving banks. Bureaus of this kind historically served the region's many small and mid sized firms, artisans and professional practices that needed outsourced bookkeeping and payroll computation before in-house computing became affordable, a service this business appears to continue in a smaller and more specialised form today. No IT load, utility power service, standby generation, technical floor area or rack count is recorded here, because a business of this description has none to publish.
profile.research_note: Expanded 2026-09-05 with OSM provenance and an explicit explanation of the Italian CED naming convention, which is the actual mechanism by which this row entered a data centre registry. OSM node/11985791319 has exactly one version, created 2024-06-16 by DabMK, entering name, addr:street, addr:housenumber, addr:postcode, addr:city, phone and telecom=data_center in a single edit, with no building geometry, consistent with transcription from a business directory rather than a survey. Italian registry facts (incorporation 1994-02-01, ATECO 63102 elaborazione dati per conto terzi, one employee, partner names Simone Bari, Susanna Bianciardi, Serena Vanni) retained from the prior ufficiocamerale.it and Paginebianche research. No capacity or power figures asserted, and none exist for a business of this size.
